subtitle: Simuka, Kanha and the birth of a Deccan dynasty from shards of stone

panels.shot: epic wide of a rocky Deccan plateau dotted with stupas and caves, Simuka and Kanha ghost-like behind carved stones
panels.action: Simuka and Kanha Satavahana stand as towering, semi-transparent figures behind weathered inscriptions and sculpted slabs at Kanaganahalli and Naneghat, the Deccan plateau stretching below under a stormy sky.

dialogue.text: In an age of fading Mauryas and rising Saka storms, two brothers—Simuka and Kanha—leave so faint a trail that even today, no one can date their throne.

i18n.hi: मौर्य ढल रहे, शक तूफान उठ रहे, ऐसे दौर में दो भाई—शिमुक और कन्ह—इतना हल्का निशान छोड़ जाते हैं कि आज तक कोई उनके तख़्त की तारीख नहीं ठोक पाया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a scholar’s hand brushing dust from an inscription in a cave
panels.action: A modern scholar’s weathered hand gently clears dust from the ancient Brahmi letters of the Naneghat inscription carved into a dark cave wall in the Western Ghats.

dialogue.text: The story begins not with a court poet, but with dust and stone in a wind-cut pass called Naneghat, where a long, careful inscription whispers a broken family tree.

i18n.hi: कहानी शुरू होती है दरबार के कवि से नहीं, धूल और पत्थर से, नानाघाट की पतली घाटी में, जहाँ एक लंबा, सधा शिलालेख टूटी हुई वंशावली फुसफुसाता है।

panels.shot: overhead view of Naneghat pass with traders, then subtle overlay of letters naming kings
panels.action: Caravans of traders climb the misty Naneghat pass, while faint overlaid Brahmi letters shimmer in the air, picking out names that hint at Simuka and Kanha.

dialogue.text: Here, in a cave above the toll-road of Naneghat, a queen carved the Satavahana line: kings, queens and princes, including a founder whose very name shifts like mist between scripts.

i18n.hi: यहीं, नानाघाट की टोल-घाटी के ऊपर गुफा में, एक रानी ने सातवाहन वंश उकेरा: राजा, रानियाँ, कुमार… और एक संस्थापक, जिसका नाम ही लिपियों में धुंध सा बदल जाता है।

panels.shot: close-up on a palm-leaf manuscript of a Purana beside a printed modern book
panels.action: A palm-leaf Purana manuscript lies beside a modern printed history on a low lamp-lit desk, their pages open to lists of kings with variant names like Shishuka and Sipraka.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the Puranas would call this first king Shishuka, Sipraka, Sindhuka. Their lists stretch and twist his reign, tying him to Kanva kings he never knew.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद पुराण उसे शिशुक, सिप्रक, सिंधुक कहेंगे। उनकी सूचियाँ उसका राज फैलाकर मोड़ देती हैं, उसे उन कण्व राजाओं से जोड़ती हैं जिन्हें वो जानता भी नहीं था।

panels.shot: dramatic split-screen style: on one side a shadowy tyrant of Jain story, on the other a calm, uncertain outline
panels.action: On one side, a smoky, exaggerated image of a cruel king from later Jain tales; on the other, a calmer, indistinct outline of Simuka, his features only half-formed, fading into inscriptions.

dialogue.text: Jain storytellers would later paint him as a tyrant toppled by righteous rebels. But the stones of the Deccan stay quiet. They give us a name, not a monster.

i18n.hi: जैन कथाकार उसे जालिम बता देंगे, धर्मयोद्धाओं के हाथों गिरा हुआ। पर दक्कन के पत्थर चुप हैं। वे हमें बस एक नाम देते हैं, कोई राक्षस नहीं।

panels.shot: low-angle on Simuka standing on a rocky outcrop overlooking the Deccan, hazy Mauryan pillars crumbling behind him
panels.action: Simuka Satavahana stands in profile on a rocky Deccan ridge, the ghostly silhouette of a crumbling Mauryan pillar behind him, as distant Saka horsemen move like shadows on the horizon.

dialogue.text: What we can see is the age. Mauryan power has thinned. Local chiefs rise and fall. From this rough plateau, a man later called Simuka gathers clan and coin, watching both Magadha and Saka frontiers.

i18n.hi: जो साफ दिखता है, वो ज़माना है। मौर्य ताकत ढीली पड़ चुकी। ठिकठिक के सरदार उठते-गिरते हैं। इसी उबड़-खाबड़ पठार से शिमुक नाम का आदमी कुल और सिक्का जुटाता है, मगध और शक दोनों सरहदों पर नज़र रखता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot of Simuka in a modest court, consulting with Kanha and elders
panels.action: Inside a simple Deccan hall with wooden pillars, Simuka confers with his younger brother Kanha and a circle of clan elders, grain jars and tax ledgers stacked nearby.

dialogue.text: We hold the passes. The caravans need us, not distant kings.

i18n.hi: दर्रे हमारे हाथ में हैं। काफ़िलों को हमारी ज़रूरत है, दूर बैठे राजाओं की नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kanaganahalli stupa complex under construction, with artisans at work
panels.action: At Kanaganahalli, artisans and laborers haul stone drums and carve reliefs around a rising stupa, scaffolding hugging its half-complete dome amid the Deccan countryside.

dialogue.text: Far to the south-east, beside the Krishna at Kanaganahalli, another trail appears centuries later. Broken slabs show portraits and labels: Siri Chimuka Satavahana… Year 16.

i18n.hi: बहुत दूर दक्षिण-पूर्व में, कृष्णा किनारे कनगनहळ्ळी पर, सदियों बाद एक और सुराग दिखता है। टूटी थप्पियों पर तस्वीरें और नाम हैं: "सिरी चिमुक सातवाहन… वर्ष 16"।

panels.shot: close-up of a Kanaganahalli sculpted slab labelled Siri Chimuka, his figure half-broken
panels.action: A carved stone slab shows a partially broken figure labeled Siri Chimuka Satavahana, his face calm, hand raised in formal gesture, the lower half of the carving missing.

dialogue.text: Here, the founder steps into the light as Siri Chimuka Satavahana—Simuka in another tongue. A real portrait, a regnal year, but still no firm birth or coronation date.

i18n.hi: यहाँ संस्थापक सामने आता है सिरी चिमुक सातवाहन के रूप में—दूसरी ज़बान का शिमुक। असली चित्र, राजवर्ष लिखा, पर अब भी न पक्की जन्म-तारीख, न गद्दीनशीनी की।

panels.shot: map-like bird’s-eye of western Deccan highlighting Naneghat, Nashik, Kanaganahalli
panels.action: A stylized bird’s-eye view of the western Deccan shows glowing points at Naneghat, Nashik, and Kanaganahalli connected by trade routes crowded with tiny moving caravans.

dialogue.text: Join the dots: Naneghat’s genealogy, Kanaganahalli’s Year 16 slab, coins scattered across the Godavari and Krishna. A dynasty emerges, not in one inscription, but in a web.

i18n.hi: अब बिंदु मिलाओ: नानाघाट की वंशावली, कनगनहळ्ळी की वर्ष 16 की थप्पी, और गोदावरी–कृष्णा पर बिखरे सिक्के। एक राजघराना उभरता है, किसी एक शिलालेख से नहीं, पूरी जाल से।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Simuka aging, handing a royal emblem to Kanha
panels.action: An older Simuka sits on a low throne, lines of age on his face, as he solemnly places a royal emblem or diadem into the hands of his younger brother Kanha, who kneels respectfully.

dialogue.text: One by one, the Puranas and Naneghat agree on one thing: after Simuka comes Kanha. Brother follows brother, and the house of Satavahana remains in family hands.

i18n.hi: एक-एक कर पुराण और नानाघाट कम से कम एक बात पर साथ हैं: शिमुक के बाद कन्ह। भाई के बाद भाई, सातवाहन घराना अपने ही हाथों में बना रहता है।

panels.shot: low-angle of Kanha leading an entourage toward a rocky hill that will be Nashik caves
panels.action: Kanha strides at the head of a small royal party towards a rocky hill overlooking the Godavari, monks and officials walking beside him under the hard Deccan sun.

dialogue.text: Kanha steps out not in myth but in his own words, at a rocky outcrop near Nashik, where caves bite into the cliff and the language of Ashoka still lingers in the air.

i18n.hi: कन्ह किवदंती में नहीं, अपने शब्दों में उतरता है, नाशिक के पास चट्टान पर, जहाँ गुफाएँ पहाड़ को काटती हैं और अशोक की बोली अब भी हवा में टंगी है।

panels.shot: close-up inside Nashik Cave 19 as a royal officer chisels Kanha’s inscription
panels.action: Inside Nashik Cave 19, a royal scribe chisels Brahmi letters into a smoothed wall while Kanha stands behind him, a Buddhist monk watching quietly from the shadows.

dialogue.text: In Cave 19, Kanha’s record calls him raja, uses Mauryan words for offices and provinces, and marks a donation to the Buddha’s community. A new power wears old administrative clothes.

i18n.hi: गुफा 19 के लेख में कन्ह खुद को राजा कहता है, मौर्य वाले ही ओहदे और सूबों के शब्द बरतता है, और बुद्ध संघ को दान दर्ज करवाता है। नई ताकत ने पुराने राजकाज के कपड़े पहन लिए हैं।

panels.shot: medium on the monk and Kanha exchanging a respectful gesture at the cave entrance
panels.action: At the cave entrance, Kanha and a robed Buddhist monk exchange respectful gestures, the valley below dotted with fields and hamlets.

dialogue.text: Let these caves shelter your monks, and our name shelter this land.

i18n.hi: इन गुफाओं में तुम्हारे भिक्षु बसें, और हमारा नाम इस धरती को आसरा दे।

panels.shot: interior scholarly shot: modern historians debating with maps and timelines behind
panels.action: Two modern historians stand before a board covered with timelines labeled with different Satavahana chronologies, maps of the Deccan, and photographs of inscriptions.

dialogue.text: Yet the question that haunts every seminar remains: did Simuka rise in the shadow of Ashoka, or a century and more later, as Saka Kshatrapas pressed the western coast?

i18n.hi: फिर भी हर सभा में मंडराता सवाल यही है: शिमुक ने अशोक की छाया में उठान ली, या एक सदी बाद, जब शक क्षत्रप पश्चिमी तट पर धकेल रहे थे?

panels.shot: split panel comparing long and short chronologies visually as two diverging timelines
panels.action: Two diverging timelines run side by side: one starting closer to the 3rd century BCE, the other near the late 1st century BCE, both converging on the same Satavahana names.

dialogue.text: The old long chronology pushed him back into the 3rd century BCE, tied to Kanvas. New readings from Kanaganahalli pull him forward, towards a late 2nd to early 1st century BCE horizon.

i18n.hi: पुरानी लंबी तारीखें उसे तीसरी सदी ईसा-पूर्व में धकेलती थीं, कण्वों से बाँधती थीं। कनगनहळ्ळी के नए पाठ उसे खींचकर देर दूसरी से आरंभिक पहली सदी ईसा-पूर्व की तरफ लाते हैं।

panels.shot: soft-focus vision of Simuka and Kanha fading into a line of later Satavahana rulers
panels.action: Simuka and Kanha’s figures stand at the head of a ghostly procession of later Satavahana rulers that stretches into the distance, their forms becoming less distinct with each step.

dialogue.text: What matters is clear even through the haze. Simuka and Kanha turn a clan into a state, a plateau into a realm, laying the ground for kings like Satakarni to come.

i18n.hi: धुंध के बीच भी असल बात साफ है। शिमुक और कन्ह एक कुल को राज बना देते हैं, पठार को राज्य, और आगे आने वाले सातकर्णि जैसे राजाओं की ज़मीन तैयार करते हैं।

panels.shot: return to the ancient stones: close-up of Kanaganahalli and Nashik inscriptions side by side
panels.action: A tight view shows photographs of the Kanaganahalli Year 16 slab and the Nashik Cave 19 inscription laid side by side on a table, a magnifying glass resting between them.

dialogue.text: Between Naneghat, Nashik and Kanaganahalli, the dates narrow, the titles align, the language shifts. But gaps remain, and the honest historian leaves them open instead of filling them with stories.

i18n.hi: नानाघाट, नाशिक और कनगनहळ्ळी के बीच तारीखें सिमटती हैं, उपाधियाँ मेल खाती हैं, ज़बान बदलती है। पर दरारें बची रहती हैं, और सच्चा इतिहासकार उन्हें भरने के बजाय खुला छोड़ देता है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide: Simuka and Kanha as silhouettes carved in stone, half in light, half in shadow
panels.action: Silhouettes of Simuka and Kanha appear as if carved on a massive stone wall, one half of their figures lit by warm sunlight, the other fading into deep shadow over the Deccan landscape.

dialogue.text: Simuka and Kanha remind us that the past is not a neat list but a broken inscription: to honour them is to read what survives, admit what does not, and let uncertainty be part of the truth.

i18n.hi: शिमुक और कन्ह याद दिलाते हैं कि इतिहास साफ-सुथरी सूची नहीं, टूटी हुई शिलालेख है: उन्हें मानना है तो जो बचा है उसे पढ़ो, जो नहीं है उसे मानो, और अनिश्चितता को सच का हिस्सा रहने दो।

title_i18n.en: The King No One Can Date
title_i18n.hi: जिस राजा को कोई तारीख नहीं दे सका

subtitle_i18n.en: Simuka, Kanha and the birth of a Deccan dynasty from shards of stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: शिमुक, कन्ह और पत्थरों के टुकड़ों से उठती दक्कन की सल्तनत
